preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 10,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= n <= 200000 for n in [n_val])
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is an integer between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(r, int) and 1 <= r <= 10**9 for r in r_list)
preconditions.description: Each layer number r_i is an integer between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(c, int) and 1 <= c <= r for c, r in zip(c_list, r_list))
preconditions.description: Each column number c_i is an integer between 1 and r_i inclusive.
All n points in a test case are distinct.
The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 200,000.

postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, str) and line.strip().isdigit() for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line contains a non-negative integer representing the minimum cost.

postconditions.expression: all(int(output_lines[i]) == min_cost(r_list_i, c_list_i) for i in range(t))
postconditions.description: For each test case i, the output integer equals the minimum cost to visit all given points starting from (1, 1), where min_cost computes the optimal path cost based on the triangle's edge activation rules and the ability to flip edges at a cost of 1.
